doc.name: A — mechanical keyboard catalogue, frozen toss, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: 65 percent hot-swap keyboard
Category: mechanical keyboard
Shot programme: frozen toss
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium mechanical keyboard product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the reflection duet in a frozen toss treatment.

SUBJECT. A 65 percent hot-swap keyboard. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Product and its reflection on a polished plane, symmetric split. Shoot on a 45mm tilt-shift with the plane tipped at f/1.8, framing for a shallow out-of-focus foreground element occluding the lower third.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with split gel lighting, teal on the shadow side and magenta on the key side. Stage the product on or against book-matched marble, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

CAMERA. Cap off, lid open or mechanism deployed, mid-use state. Shoot on a 35mm reportage at f/2, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with north-facing window light with a black v-flat for negative fill. Stage the product on or against book-matched marble, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.
